title: Japanese Surveys of the Chinese Herpetofauna During the Japanese Invasion of China
content: During the Japanese invasion of China (1894 - 1945), the Japanese carried out compre-hensive surveys of natural resources in China, including amphibians and reptiles that this article focuses on. The surveys of herpetofauna were conducted by dozens of Japanese scholars from about a dozen Japanese universities and academic institutions. The surveys’ results were presented in the books, monograph, reports, articles, and lectures at the time. Now, about 100 years later, with the gradual release of these historical documents, it is possible to conduct research on the history of colonial science during the Japanese invasion of China. A total of 93 species, comprising 25 amphibians (4 Caudata + 21 Anura) and 68 reptiles (2 Crocodylia + 7 Testudines + 15 Lacertilia + 44 Serpentes), were discovered and recorded in those original documents. These 93 species account for 17.2% of the 540 species (168 amphibians + 372 reptiles) recorded in China before 1945, and the proportions of amphibians and reptiles were 14.9% (25/168) and 18.3% (68/372) respectively. In the present study, those names of species from approximately 100 years ago and their rec-orded distribution locations in the historical documents were listed and compared with their current scientific names and distribution areas. We also discussed the changes in taxonomy and natural history information of some species. This article aims to provide a new perspective for understanding the colonial nature of Japanese scientific expeditions to China and some basic information of the science history studies of Chinese herpetology.
